page: Microsoft Azure E192ids_v6 is an isolated, local-disk-enabled server instance belonging to the Edsv6 family. It features 192 vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It is equipped with 1832.0 GB of RAM, yielding 9.54 GB of memory per core, and includes 11339 GB of local storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 158923.19 and a PassMark CPU score of 122297.6. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, registering top-tier read-only small block speeds of 12329.57 GB/sec and large block write speeds of 187.08 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1929.19, placing it in the average tier. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in cryptographic and vector calculations.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and massive local storage capacity, this instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale databases, and data-dense applications. It demonstrates top-tier database performance with 35481.69 operations per second in PassMark database benchmarks and 179.31 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. The high density of compute and memory resources provides qualitative cost efficiency for consolidated enterprise workloads, though the lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy parallel deep learning training.
description: Microsoft Azure E192ids_v6 is an isolated, memory-optimized server instance from the Edsv6 family, powered by a 192-vCPU Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 1832.0 GB of RAM and 11339 GB of local storage, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 158923.19, and exceptional memory bandwidth, reaching 12329.57 GB/sec for cached small blocks. It also supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. While single-core performance remains in the average tier, its massive memory capacity and high-speed local storage make it highly efficient for large-scale database operations, Redis deployments, and enterprise-level data processing.
